Residential

Concrete Driveways

Your driveway carries vehicles every day and frames the front of your home. We install new concrete driveways and replace worn, cracked, or settled ones, and we treat the work below the surface as seriously as the finish on top.

A driveway project usually begins with removing the old surface where needed, excavating to the right depth, and building a compacted gravel base. Forms are set to the planned grade so water drains away from the garage and the house. Reinforcement is placed to suit the project before the concrete is poured, finished, and given time to cure.

  • New driveway installation
  • Driveway replacement
  • Residential driveway slabs
  • Base preparation and compaction
  • Drainage and slope planning
  • Broom and smooth surface finishes

Project considerations

  • Driveway width, length, and connection to the street or apron
  • Existing concrete or asphalt that needs to be removed
  • Soil conditions and how deep the base needs to be
  • Slope, and where water should drain
  • Vehicle loads, including trailers or heavier vehicles
  • Permit or right-of-way requirements for apron work

Outdoor living

Concrete Patios

A patio extends your living space outdoors: a place for the grill, a dining table, or a quiet morning coffee. We build concrete patios sized and shaped around how you actually plan to use the space.

Standard broom-finished or smooth-troweled concrete is a durable, practical choice for most backyards. Decorative and stamped finishes can be discussed where available for your project, along with custom shapes, curves, and clean connections to existing steps, walkways, or doors.

  • Backyard patios
  • Outdoor entertainment spaces
  • Standard concrete patios
  • Decorative and stamped options, where available
  • Custom shapes and layouts
  • Tie-ins to existing walks and steps

Project considerations

  • How the space will be used and what it needs to hold
  • Slope away from the house foundation
  • Access for equipment and concrete delivery to the backyard
  • Connections to doors, steps, or existing surfaces
  • Finish choice and slip resistance
  • Trees, roots, and nearby landscaping

Residential

Concrete Sidewalks & Walkways

Walkways lead people to your door, around your home, and through your yard. A well-built walk feels steady underfoot, drains properly, and lines up cleanly with the surfaces around it.

We install residential walkways, front entry paths, and garden walks, straight or curved, and replace sidewalk sections that have cracked, heaved, or become trip hazards. Finishes are chosen for practical traction through Kentucky’s wet and freezing months.

  • Residential walkways
  • Front entry paths
  • Garden walkways
  • Sidewalk replacement
  • Straight and curved layouts
  • Practical traction finishes

Project considerations

  • Path width and route across the property
  • Transitions to steps, porches, and driveways
  • Tree roots that may have lifted existing sections
  • Control joint spacing
  • Drainage along the edges of the path
  • City requirements where public sidewalk is involved

Structural base

Concrete Slabs & Pads

Sheds, storage buildings, HVAC units, generators, and equipment all need a level, solid base. We pour concrete pads and general-purpose slabs sized to what will sit on them.

A good slab starts with a level, compacted base and accurate forms. Thickness and reinforcement are planned around the expected load, and the surface is finished to suit its purpose, whether that is anchoring a building or providing a clean, flat work area.

  • Equipment pads
  • Storage building pads
  • Shed pads
  • Utility pads
  • General-purpose concrete slabs
  • Leveling and base preparation

Project considerations

  • What will sit on the slab, and how much it weighs
  • Exact dimensions required by the building or equipment maker
  • Anchor bolts or other embedded items
  • Existing ground level and how much fill is needed
  • Distance from property lines and other structures
  • Access for the concrete truck or a pump

Interior slab

Garage Floors

A garage floor takes vehicle weight, dropped tools, temperature swings, and whatever drips off the car in winter. We install new garage slabs and concrete floors with careful attention to the base, thickness, and finish.

Reinforcement, slab thickness, and joint layout are planned for how the floor will be used. The surface is finished smooth and even, with a gentle pitch toward the door where the design calls for it, so water doesn’t collect inside.

  • New garage slabs
  • Concrete floor installation
  • Reinforcement planning
  • Control joint layout
  • Smooth trowel finishes
  • Pitch toward the door where required

Project considerations

  • Attached or detached garage, and the existing foundation
  • Vehicle and storage loads
  • Reinforcement and vapor barrier needs
  • Floor drains or existing utilities
  • The transition at the door and driveway apron
  • Curing time before vehicles can park

Business & property

Commercial Concrete Flatwork

Business owners, property managers, and general contractors need flatwork that is built carefully and with as little disruption as possible to customers and tenants. We take on small commercial concrete projects with the same attention we bring to a residential job.

Work includes commercial sidewalks, building entryways, concrete pads for equipment or dumpsters, small commercial slabs, and general property improvements. Access, staging, and pour timing are coordinated around the property’s operations wherever possible.

  • Commercial sidewalks
  • Entryways
  • Equipment and dumpster pads
  • Small commercial slabs
  • Property improvements
  • Coordination with GCs and managers

Project considerations

  • Keeping entrances and walkways usable during the work
  • Accessibility requirements at entries and walks
  • Heavier traffic and load requirements
  • Specifications from an architect or general contractor
  • Scheduling around business hours
  • Permits and inspections

Also part of the work

Concrete Steps & Entryways

Front steps, stoops, and entry landings connect your walkway or driveway to the door. Riser heights, landing size, and drainage are planned so the entry is comfortable and safe to use. Availability depends on the project’s design and site; we’ll discuss what’s practical at the estimate.

Concrete Removal

Many projects begin by breaking out and hauling away an old, cracked, or settled surface. Removal is usually quoted as part of a replacement so preparation and the new pour are planned together.

The finish is the last step, not the first

Every service above follows the same sequence: prepare the site and base, place the concrete carefully, then finish and cure it properly. Edges, joints, and transitions get hand attention, because they are where most concrete problems start.
